question: What electrical state do cardiac cells maintain across their membrane at rest?
explanation: Cardiac cells maintain a stable negative electrical charge inside the cell membrane until an impulse triggers activation. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: A re-entrant cardiac circuit leads to an arrhythmia because of...

options.A: Continuous circling of an electrical impulse
options.B: Excessive potassium loss in the blood
options.C: Total failure of the sinoatrial node
options.D: Sudden stoppage of all heart valves

explanation: Abnormal conduction pathways allow impulses to loop repeatedly, short-circuiting normal heart pacing. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: Class III antiarrhythmic drugs primarily affect which ion channel?
explanation: Class III drugs block potassium efflux, which prolongs the repolarization phase of the action potential. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h2)

question: The Vaughan Williams system categorizes antiarrhythmic drugs based on their...

options.B: Speed of absorption in the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Electrophysiological mechanism on the action potential
options.D: Metabolic breakdown by the liver enzymes

explanation: Drugs are grouped according to how they alter the specific ionic currents governing the cardiac action potential. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h2)

question: Class I antiarrhythmic drugs exert their primary action by blocking which ion?
explanation: Class I drugs bind to sodium channels to suppress the rapid upstroke of the cardiac action potential. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h3)

question: A patient receiving a Class IC drug like flecainide must be monitored closely for...

options.A: Severe shortening of the PR interval

explanation: Class IC agents produce strong sodium blockade which significantly slows electrical conduction velocity through the heart. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary cellular target for Class II antiarrhythmic drugs?
explanation: Class II drugs are beta-blockers that inhibit catecholamine action at beta-1 receptors in cardiac tissue. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h4)

question: How do beta-blockers help treat fast heart arrhythmias?

options.A: By blocking sodium entry during the initial action potential
options.B: By opening peripheral blood vessels to drop blood pressure
options.C: By speeding up the repolarization phase across ventricles
options.D: By decreasing SA node automaticity and slowing AV conduction

explanation: Blocking sympathetic tone reduces the firing rate of the pacemaker cells and slows conduction through the AV junction. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h4)

question: Class III antiarrhythmic medications primarily prolong which phase of the cardiac cycle?
explanation: By blocking potassium channels, these drugs delay the outflow of potassium, which lengthens repolarization and the refractory period. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why does prolonging the cardiac refractory period help stop re-entrant arrhythmias?

options.A: It converts all cardiac muscle cells into smooth muscle tissue
options.B: It keeps tissue unresponsive long enough for errant loops to die out
options.C: It prevents the SA node from ever generating another impulse
options.D: It speeds up blood flow through the coronary arteries instantly

explanation: Extending the time cells remain refractory prevents premature re-excitation, breaking the circuit sustaining the arrhythmia. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which two drugs belong to the Class IV calcium channel blocker category?
explanation: Verapamil and diltiazem are the non-dihydropyridine calcium antagonists used for their cardiac rate-control properties. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary electrophysiological effect of Class IV drugs on the heart?

options.C: Slowing conduction through the AV node

explanation: Calcium channel blockers depress calcium currents in nodal tissue, slowing down conduction speed through the AV junction. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the drug of choice administered via rapid IV push to treat paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia?
explanation: Adenosine briefly blocks AV nodal conduction, effectively breaking re-entrant loops causing PSVT. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h7)

question: Magnesium sulfate is uniquely indicated for managing which specific rhythm disturbance?
explanation: Magnesium stabilizes the cardiac membrane and is the primary treatment for this specific polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h7)

question: A patient taking a medication that prolongs the QT interval must be monitored for the development of...
explanation: Excessive QT prolongation increases the risk of triggering life-threatening ventricular rhythms like Torsades de Pointes. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why is baseline electrolyte assessment crucial before starting antiarrhythmic therapy?

options.A: Abnormal potassium or magnesium levels can trigger or worsen arrhythmias
options.B: Electrolytes determine how fast the drug is absorbed in the stomach
options.C: Mineral balance dictates liver metabolism speed for all cardiac drugs
options.D: Normal sodium levels prevent allergic reactions to the medication

explanation: Electrolyte imbalances directly alter cardiac cell resting potentials and reduce the effectiveness or safety of antiarrhythmic drugs. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h8)
